entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Serenus of Antinoupolis was a Greek mathematician from the Late Antique Thebaid in Roman Egypt.

Born in the 3rd century AD, Serenus is known for his work on conic sections and his contributions to the development of mathematical astronomy.

He was a prominent figure in the Theban mathematician community, collaborating with other notable scholars such as Pappus of Alexandria.

Serenus' work had a lasting impact on the field of mathematics, influencing later scholars such as Ptolemy and Archimedes.

A testament to his significance, Serenus' writings were preserved in the Theban manuscript collection, providing valuable insights into the mathematical achievements of the Late Antique period.

In the words of historian and scholar, 'Serenus' contributions to mathematics are a shining example of the intellectual prowess of the Theban mathematicians, whose work continues to inspire and enlighten scholars to this day.'
